United States Department of the Interior
1792.2 (220)
BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT WASHINGTON, D.C. 20240
MAY 1 0 1972
Memorandum
To:
Chief, Office of Environmental Quality
Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
From:
Director, Bureau of Land Management
Subject: Review of Draft Environmental Statement for
H.R. 13111 - Endangered Species Legislation
We have reviewed the subject draft statement. The draft deals adequately with the complex nature of the many endangered species ecosystems and their relationship with man. We offer the following comments for your consideration in preparation of the final statement.
1. The proposed legislation, H.R. 13111, would expand the authority of the Secretary of the Interior to conserve, protect, restore, and propagate species or subspecies of fish and wildlife that he lists as threatened with extinction or is likely in the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction. A discussion would be helpful of the indirect impact this expanded authority may have on the freedom of the States to control and regulate the capturing, taking and processing of resident fish and wildlife by the public within State boundaries.
2. Provisions in subsection 2(c)(2) would require the Secretary, after making such determination, to publish a list of endangered species, indicating in the list whether such species is threatened with extinction or is likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction and, in either case, over what portion of the range of such species this condition exists. Since this new authority establishes a new procedure, a discussion of the old procedure and what portion of that procedure will be dropped would assist the reader in understanding the new procedure the Secretary will follow. For instance, will the new procedure still list species of presently used categories, such as the rare category?
In Senger
